analysis:
The PR adds only a test file (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Tools/StructuredForcedToolAdmissionTests.swift, lines 1-381). It has no production code change, so it adds no runtime attack surface and weakens no control. The tests use only static fixtures and scripted model output. They use an invalid coordinator URL (coordinator.invalid), real network connections are never opened, and they handle no secrets or keys.

Security-relevant behavior the tests assert, which supports the T-007/T-008 style fail-closed posture:
- Registration and models_update advertise toolConstraintModels only for exact (id, modelType) admitted builds (lines 71-100), and a replaced build is revoked on the next update.
- Forced required/named tool_choice is withheld until validated (lines 105-124, 297-327). The router emits only empty-content parsed events.
- Prose, wrong-name, undeclared, schema-invalid, extra-property and over-count calls are refused as toolChoiceViolation (lines 166-247).
- Harmony (gpt_oss) is not advertised and refuses forced choice (lines 126-135).

Limits: the production policies (ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy, ToolChoicePromptPolicy, ToolConstraintValidation, NativeToolStreamRouter, CoordinatorClientCodec) are not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the tests match production behavior or that the admitted list in production matches the test's list. Test results prove the serving contract, not model call quality or provider honesty (T-007 remains an accepted limitation). Nothing here touches the prefix-cache threat T-041 or the attestation and authorization threats.
